editorial:
Imagine jumping back into the chaotic streets of Tokyo three years after the main story ended. You get to see Makoto again, but he is in a rough spot. His mom sold the family shop, leaving him homeless and drifting through the city. The vibe is a wild mix of gritty street crime and quirky humor. You will find yourself following Makoto as he gets caught up in a creepy mystery involving a bone smasher who targets people living on the streets. It feels like a reunion with old friends, but the stakes are much higher and the streets feel a bit more dangerous than before.

The acting is top-notch and the pacing keeps you on your toes without feeling rushed. You will love how the mystery unfolds, though some parts of the plot get a bit messy. If you enjoy crime dramas that do not take themselves too seriously, this is for you. It is a great way to spend an afternoon if you want something with a bit of edge.
endingExplained: The mystery wraps up when the identity of the bone smasher is finally revealed. It turns out the attacks were linked to a dark cycle of betrayal and revenge within the street community. After a tense showdown, the truth comes out and the culprit is stopped. Makoto manages to find some peace and closure regarding his family situation, proving that even when you hit rock bottom, you can still find your way back up.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves street-level crime mysteries with a touch of comedy.
